task: Add `parse_age(value)` to app/users.py. It accepts an int, or a string of decimal digits with optional surrounding whitespace, and returns the age as an int. Valid ages are 0 to 150 inclusive. Anything else (other types, booleans, non-digit strings, negative numbers, ages over 150) must be rejected with `ValidationError`.
why:
I picked c3 because it is the most maintainable of three otherwise equivalent changes. All three meet the request, use the repo's existing `ValidationError`, and call `record_rejection` before raising, as the policy in `app/audit.py` requires. All three also reject bools and non-ASCII digits correctly; c1 does it with `isascii()`, c2 and c3 with the `[0-9]+` regex.
c3 handles the bool exclusion and the type check in one branch, appends `parse_age` after `parse_name`, and has the shortest correct body.
Runner-up c1 is just as correct but longer: it repeats the reject-and-record code across branches, which costs it on minimal size. c2 puts `parse_age` above the existing `parse_name` instead of appending it, and gives bools their own separate branch.
